claims.explanation: Crizotinib is a multi-kinase inhibitor whose selective killing is best explained by dependence on its targets ALK, MET, or ROS1, typically through genomic activation such as gene fusion, amplification, or mutation. The most sensitive lines likely harbor MET amplification/mutation or ROS1/ALK fusions, while resistant lines lack these alterations or have bypass signaling. The observed enrichment of MET mutation in sensitive lines and absence of target alterations in resistant lines supports this mechanism.

features.basis: Crizotinib inhibits MET; MET mutations/amplification can drive oncogenic dependence
ALK fusions are the canonical crizotinib sensitivity biomarker
ROS1 rearrangements confer crizotinib sensitivity
High MET expression/amplification may increase dependence on MET signaling
High ALK expression may indicate ALK-driven tumors
High ROS1 expression may indicate ROS1-driven tumors
EGFR mutations may drive resistance to crizotinib through bypass signaling
KRAS mutations may activate bypass pathways reducing crizotinib efficacy
BRAF mutations may drive MAPK pathway activation bypassing ALK/MET inhibition
PTEN loss may activate PI3K/AKT survival signaling reducing drug sensitivity
NF1 loss may activate RAS/MAPK pathway conferring resistance
TP53 mutations may impair apoptosis and reduce drug response
